sources.title: Baton (desktop) home
sources.locator: Baton is now Komla; FAQ: existing subscription and supported agents; Run agents on a remote machine
sources.finding: The official Baton page explicitly says Baton relaunched as Komla, free and open source with no account or limits. The FAQ says agents use their own CLI login or API key and Baton does not charge for tokens.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) readme
sources.finding: Komla documents public macOS, Windows beta and Linux beta downloads, terminal-based coding agents, local or SSH worktrees, its CLI, schedulers and a free application with no vendor account.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) docs/FEATURES.md
sources.locator: Agent support; Git Worktree-Based Workspaces; Built-in Git GUI; Remote Workspaces; Automations
sources.finding: Agent presets have configurable open/continue/prompt commands. Workspaces are Git worktrees, with local or SSH execution. The Git menu supports branch operations. Scheduled runs create new workspaces, locally while the app is open or by cron on an SSH host.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) src/main/services/agent-preset.service.ts
sources.locator: Built-in preset definitions and open/continue/prompt command fields
sources.finding: The preset service supplies terminal launch definitions for named coding CLIs, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor CLI, Pi and others. This is terminal process integration, not a shared model-provider endpoint.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) docs/CLI.md
sources.locator: komla launch; terminals/read/send/wait; example launching Codex to review src/x.ts
sources.finding: The product CLI starts an agent in a workspace or another terminal tab, waits for its turn or attention state, reads its screen and sends a follow-up. These commands are also taught through bundled skills.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) LICENSE
sources.finding: The inspected Komla application source is MIT-licensed. The README reserves the Komla name and logo separately.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) package.json
sources.finding: The application package uses Electron for the desktop client.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) docs/ANALYTICS.md
sources.finding: Packaged app installs and daily heartbeats are enabled by default, while identified usage analytics require opt-in. Settings General Privacy controls the usage-data level and a separate crash-report toggle. DO_NOT_TRACK or KOMLA_TELEMETRY can disable collection.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) src/main/services/telemetry.service.ts
sources.finding: The telemetry sender skips unpackaged development builds and skips heartbeat collection when the telemetry level is off. It sends heartbeat requests through the app API worker when enabled.

sources.title: Baton (desktop) src/shared/lib/telemetry-level.ts
sources.finding: The telemetry-level helper maps config to off, anonymous or usage and keeps anonymous collection distinct from opt-in usage.
